Order Order

This is an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
 2.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned  counsel for the State and learned counsel for the  opposite party no.2.
 3.

The petitioner is an accused in connection with  Narasinghpur P.S. Case No.156 of 2023 corresponding  to G.R. Case No.174 of 2023 registered under Sections  341/354/354-C/328/376(3)/506/34 of the IPC read  with Section 6 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court  of leaned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court  under POCSO Act, Cuttack.
The petitioner had  approached the learned Additional Sessions Judge-  cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Cuttack praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 22.12.2023, rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the plea of bail of the petitioner is not pending before any other Court, except the present one.

sentences.text: The petitioner had one sided love with the victim and used to harass her while she was returning from the School.
On 07.06.2023, the co-accused Pinki came to the house of the informant and invited the victim to their house to which the victim denied.
On 09.06.2023 while the victim was returning from tuition, she was called by said Pinki to their house and she was given chocolate to eat.
After eating the chocolate, the victim became senseless and when she regained her senses, she found herself on a bed in naked condition with the petitioner.
It is further alleged that the victim had threatened by the petitioner not to disclose the fact to anybody.

Hence,
the F.I.R.
5.
Learned counsel for the State submits that the statement of the victim has been recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.

In her statement, she has stated that on the date of incident, her cousin sister,
namely, Pinki had given two chocolates to her.
After taking chocolates, she became unconscious.
When she regained her senses, she found her in a naked condition and the present petitioner was lying over her.
She somehow pushed the petitioner and at that stage, the petitioner has threatened her not to disclose the fact to anyone.
6. I have perused the medical evidence, which indicates that there was no recent sign and symptom of sexual intercourse.
7. Taking into consideration the period of custody since 20.10.2023 and the nature of accusation, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

The prosecution is given liberty to move application before the Court below for cancellation of bail,
if the petitioner violates any of the conditions of the bail granted to him.
9. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
